name: Garfield Rack
description:
Garfield Rack is cop country. Always was, even before Meridian 88 absorbed Chicago's Southwest Side and reorganized everything into tiers and jurisdictions. Old Garfield Ridge was where the city's police officers, firefighters, and municipal workers bought homes, raised families, and built a community defined by the particular solidarity of people who carry badges. When the megacity transition came, that identity didn't dissolve -- it calcified. Garfield Rack became the residential stronghold for Meridian's enforcement class: Axiom Security operatives, corporate jurisdiction officers, fire suppression contractors, and the various private police forces that keep the tier system running. They live here, in neat rows of reinforced bungalows with security-grade neural mesh and perimeter monitoring that makes the neighborhood effectively self-surveilling.

Midway, the old airport, is the district's geographic anchor and its economic engine. The runways were converted decades ago into a logistics hub -- automated cargo drones launch and land in continuous rotation, distributing goods across Meridian's commercial network. The hub employs thousands, most of them Rack residents, in operations, security, and maintenance roles. The drone traffic is constant overhead, a mechanical migration pattern that residents have learned to sleep through. The noise complaints stopped years ago, not because the noise stopped, but because complaining would mean admitting that the thing that employs you is also the thing that's ruining your hearing.

The Rack's relationship with the rest of Meridian is complicated by the fact that its residents are the enforcement mechanism for a system they didn't design and don't fully benefit from. Tier 3 is the ceiling here -- comfortable enough, with corporate health coverage and retirement accounts, but forever below the Tier 4 and 5 executives whose orders they carry out. It creates a specific psychology: loyalty to the system paired with resentment of the system, expressed as a ferocious insularity. Rack residents take care of Rack residents. They don't trust the Spire, they don't sympathize with the Shelf, and they don't talk about what happens on shift. The bungalows are well-maintained. The lawns are trimmed. The silence about certain things is absolute.

sights: Rows of reinforced bungalows with security-grade perimeter arrays -- suburbia with teeth
Midway logistics hub visible from everywhere -- automated cargo drones in constant flight patterns
Off-duty enforcement personnel in civilian clothes that don't quite hide the augment profiles
Block watch holographics rotating at intersections -- community surveillance branded as community pride
Memorial walls listing Rack residents killed in enforcement operations across the city
sounds: Cargo drone engines -- a constant industrial buzz that defines the district's acoustic baseline
The click and hum of perimeter security systems cycling through detection modes
Police scanner frequencies bleeding from open windows -- off-duty but never fully off
Quiet conversations on front porches, voices kept low from professional habit
Shift change sirens from the Midway hub, marking time for the entire neighborhood
smells: Drone fuel exhaust from the Midway hub -- kerosene-adjacent, omnipresent on south wind days
Fresh-cut synthetic turf from fastidiously maintained yards
Gun oil and augment lubricant -- the smell of people who maintain their tools
Bar food from the enforcement-class taverns along the main drag
atmosphere.feel: Controlled. Not the corporate control of the Meridian Core, but the self-imposed control of people who spend their working lives managing other people's chaos and need their home to be the opposite. There is warmth here, but it's conditional -- extended to those who belong and withheld from those who don't. The Rack feels like a fist that's learned to relax at home but never quite unclenches.

demographics: Approximately 40,000 residents, overwhelmingly Tier 3 enforcement-class families. Historically Irish, Polish, and Latino -- old Garfield Ridge demographics persisting through the megacity transition. A closed community in the sociological sense: intermarriage within the enforcement class is common, outsider settlement is rare.
economy: Midway logistics hub employment and enforcement-class salaries form the economic base. A secondary economy of enforcement equipment suppliers, augment maintenance shops catering to security-grade hardware, and service businesses that cater to shift workers.
power_structure: The Rack is informally governed by the Enforcement Veterans Association, an organization that functions as neighborhood council, mutual aid society, and lobby group. Axiom Security has a district liaison office but treads carefully -- the Rack's residents are Axiom's workforce, and they know their leverage.
dangers: Outsiders are noticed immediately and tracked through overlapping residential surveillance
Off-duty enforcement personnel who respond to perceived threats with professional-grade reflexes
The institutional silence about enforcement abuses -- asking the wrong questions gets you flagged
Midway drone traffic -- the flight paths are mapped but the drones don't stop for pedestrians
Getting caught between the Rack's loyalty to its residents and its loyalty to the system
opportunities: Enforcement-class contacts who know how Axiom Security operates from the inside
Midway logistics hub access -- cargo manifests, shipping routes, and the occasional misdirected package
The Enforcement Veterans Association has institutional memory about every major security operation in Meridian's history
Off-duty officers who are willing to trade information when they're angry enough at the system they serve
story_hooks: An Axiom Security internal affairs investigation is targeting Rack residents -- and the Enforcement Veterans Association is closing ranks in ways that suggest what's being protected is bigger than any individual

A Midway logistics hub worker has discovered that certain cargo drone flights don't appear on any manifest -- they launch at 0300, carry no corporate markings, and their flight paths end in the Indiana Exclusion Zone
Kyle needs information that only someone inside the enforcement class would have, and the only person willing to talk lives in the Rack and is running out of time
frequented_by: Off-duty Axiom Security operatives and corporate jurisdiction officers
Midway logistics hub workers and drone maintenance crews
Enforcement equipment dealers servicing security-grade augments
Rack families who've lived here for three generations and intend to stay for three more
The occasional outsider who walks too confidently and leaves too quickly
